items.title: Publish and maintain the design baseline
acceptance: Product, UX, business, system, data, API, security, engineering, ADR, and release documents have a named canonical location.
Decisions marked proposed are not represented as implemented or accepted.
No private/customer artifacts are in the public source scope.

items.title: Qualify runtime and framework candidates
acceptance: Record exact versions, licenses, Node compatibility, install and upgrade shape for candidates.

Exercise API/OpenAPI, DB migration, Temporal replay, connector contract, ObjectStack-native view rendering with only a narrow app-composition manifest, AG-UI and MCP auth boundary using a synthetic vertical spike.
Update ADR-0002 and other affected ADRs with evidence and accepted/rejected choices.

items.title: Validate task-first setup with synthetic maintenance example
acceptance: Synthetic work-order and inventory examples cover success, ambiguity, stale source, partial failure, and unresolved rule.
At least five formative target-user sessions observe setup and task-state comprehension; findings and changes are recorded.
No real customer records or credentials are required.

items.title: Define and validate immutable executable business package
acceptance: Release envelope references qualified ObjectStack-native metadata by version/digest and defines only the missing task evidence/source-mapping/action-safety extensions.

ObjectStack's native validator checks native object/action/permission/view metadata; platform validation rejects unresolved extension references, incompatible mappings, unconfirmed required decisions, unsafe connector claims and duplicate extension IDs.
Publishing creates an immutable semantic version and canonical digest; a change creates a new revision.

items.title: Build connection catalog and read connector ports
acceptance: Connection, catalog, mapping and capability grant are separate versioned records.
Connection verification checks identity mode, scope, schema fingerprint and limits; URL reachability alone is insufficient.
Connector contract supports cancellation, bounded pagination, timeout, provenance and typed unsupported-feature errors.

items.title: Implement OIDC identity and default-deny authorization kernel
acceptance: Production identity is verified OIDC; development mock cannot start in production mode.
Authorization resolves current principal and denies by default on query, publish, approve and submit.
Browser session, CSRF, session expiry, revocation and service-client scope are documented and verified.

items.title: Implement authorized query kernel with provenance and budgets
acceptance: Queries resolve only declared package capability IDs and filter arguments against schemas.
Authorization occurs before data reaches an Agent; output preserves source, mapping revision, freshness, completeness and sensitivity.
Per-source and per-run time, byte, row, page, concurrency and context budgets are enforced; partial and truncated outcomes are explicit.

items.title: Deliver task-first builder and readiness matrix
acceptance: A user can choose the maintenance template, inspect/edit a draft, review evidence and identify who owns each blocker.
Read, draft, preview, submit and recovery readiness are separate.
Unknown, conflict, stale and partial states cannot be silently rendered as ordinary success.

items.title: Render qualified native task views and controlled app composition
acceptance: Generated view/app declarations reuse qualified ObjectStack-native metadata; any narrow app-composition manifest references native component/view/query/action IDs and introduces no second business/view/permission schema.
Validation rejects arbitrary script, unknown component, forbidden field and cross-release reference.
Published spec is immutable; runtime evaluates current permissions; action confirmation uses canonical server effect data.

items.title: Add single-agent runtime and governed MCP surfaces
acceptance: One harness/provider adapter proposes only capabilities currently granted to the run.
Agent, UI, public API and platform MCP use the same kernel and typed result model.
External MCP metadata and Skill content do not grant access; server registry enforces pinned schema, host allowlist, auth and budgets.

items.title: Implement action intent, effect preview and decision binding
acceptance: Server canonicalizes operation, target, args, release, source preconditions and effect digest.
Requester confirmation and business approval are different records and bind to same effect digest and current policy.
Changed effect, revoked access, expired approval or connector drift blocks submission.

items.title: Implement one durable source command and reconciliation path
acceptance: Action ledger and outbox commit atomically before orchestration starts.
One Temporal worker owns side effects; duplicate deliveries are safe and source correlation is retained.
Simulated source-commit/response-loss resolves by source query or reaches manual review; unsafe automatic retry is impossible.

items.title: Complete security, isolation and recovery release gate
acceptance: Threat scenarios have executed evidence, owners and residual-risk disposition.
Secret scan, dependency/license/SBOM, permission-revocation, prompt injection, MCP poisoning, replay, concurrency and recovery scenarios pass.
No production-write claim appears before the release gate is met.

items.title: Package supported single-organization self-hosted deployment
acceptance: Clean Linux installation starts through documented Compose path with health checks and no default production secret.
OIDC, model provider, secret manager, backup/restore, upgrade and disable procedures are exercised.
Supported architecture, versions, data retention and operational limits are in release notes.

items.title: Validate a second business domain without kernel fork
acceptance: Employee equipment-request workflow uses existing package, auth, query, action and AppSpec abstractions.
New requirements and abstractions are justified by measured gaps; no copy of the maintenance kernel is made.
Second-domain install and user-feedback evidence is recorded.

items.title: Validate contributor and external installation experience
acceptance: Independent developer follows docs to add a synthetic connector or task template.
Independent user can install, upgrade, restore, configure OIDC, and report a blocker without maintainer-only knowledge.
External feedback updates documentation and prioritization.

items.title: Deliver low-friction connector onboarding and compatibility report
acceptance: Admin can import a supported OpenAPI document or configure a REST endpoint and choose an explicitly safe read operation.
Connection report separately shows reachability, authentication, schema discovery, read verification, operation scopes, limits, support tier, and known gaps.
Credentials are stored by secret reference and never enter Agent context or AppSpec artifacts.
Import and test paths enforce host allowlists, SSRF protections, request/response limits, timeouts, and do not execute source writes.
One described and one manually configured synthetic source pass the connector contract suite; unsupported protocol/auth cases identify the extension route.

items.title: Build evidence-backed ontology authoring workbench
acceptance: Authorized schema and synthetic business files can produce proposed ObjectStack-native objects, relations, mappings, rules, and exceptions without defining a parallel ontology schema.
Each proposal retains source/page/path evidence and an explicit provenance state; Agent confidence cannot promote it to confirmed.
Users can inspect and edit the model through graph/table/form views without authoring ontology code.
Business owner confirmation is attributable, versioned, and distinct from publisher approval or source grants.
File access, extraction, retention, deletion, MIME/size limits, and untrusted-content handling are explicit.

items.title: Implement visual model validation, cases, and read-only dry run
acceptance: Workbench displays source-to-domain mappings, graph relationships, conflicts, package diff, test cases, and actionable blockers.
Validator checks structural references, types/units, required confirmations, sensitivity/authorization, bounded rules, and capability safety.
Synthetic cases cover positive, negative, edge, stale, partial, conflict, denied access, and connector failure.
Connected-data trial uses authorized reads only; instrumentation/evidence proves the action execute port was not invoked.
Publish is blocked for required unresolved or failed gates and reports the responsible role and affected capability.

items.title: Add action automation modes and policy simulator
acceptance: Every action has one explicit mode and a versioned policy covering actor, environment, effect bounds, evidence freshness, source safety, expiry, budget, and separation of duties.
Server reevaluates current policy/authorization at each transition and dispatch; clients and models cannot upgrade mode.
Simulator reports routing and exact failed guard across safe, denied, stale, conflicting, expired, revoked, connector-drift, and unknown-outcome cases.
Guarded autonomous mode is rejected unless business-owner/publisher approval, deterministic bounds, and connector idempotency/reconciliation evidence exist.
Audit identifies policy revision, guards and the decision path; simulator output itself grants no authority.

items.title: Build and promote immutable generated task app releases
acceptance: Qualified ObjectStack-native view/component metadata supports the demonstrated conventional and Agent-collaboration pages; any app manifest is limited to composition and uses an allowlisted renderer registry.
AG-UI carries Agent interaction events but does not define the canonical app schema, action authorization, or release artifact.

Publisher produces reproducible signed/digested OCI or static release with pinned native metadata, narrow composition manifest, extension package, policy, component catalog and API compatibility references.
Same artifact digest is promoted across environments; runtime secret references, grants, identity and permissions remain environment-specific and current.
Generated apps pass role simulation, keyboard/accessibility, denied-binding, revocation, and clean deployment checks.

items.title: Add typed graph-relation and time-series read capabilities
acceptance: Graph relations use typed object/edge IDs, source authority and bounded traversal; arbitrary Cypher/SPARQL or unbounded expansion is rejected.
Time-series query contract requires UTC interval semantics, unit, aggregation/resolution, quality/gap metadata, source watermark and maximum points.
Both data shapes enforce the current principal/source scope before model context, budgets, provenance and freshness metadata.
Synthetic conformance cases cover unit conversion, timezone boundaries, missing intervals, stale watermarks, denied rows/edges, and traversal/point-limit overflow.
No graph/time-series database is added without measured workload evidence; any new dependency or public contract has a reviewed ADR.

items.title: Deliver a constrained private-network connector gateway profile
acceptance: Gateway initiates outbound mTLS only; no inbound tunnel, arbitrary port-forwarding, shell, browser or package installation is available.
Each connection has a destination allowlist, explicit source identity mode, local secret reference and least-privilege connector workload identity.
Platform sends only signed/versioned capability requests; gateway rechecks grants and limits and returns provenance-bearing bounded results.
Revocation, lost heartbeat, expired certificate, adapter signature failure, and unexpected destination all fail closed and stop new calls.
A customer can upgrade/roll back a pinned gateway build and connector without losing audit/evidence; compromise and SSRF scenarios are exercised before production use.
